B15C001.summary: Janamejaya asks Vaisampayana how the Pandavas treated the defeated old king Dhritarashtra and Gandhari after recovering their kingdom, and how many years they ruled. Vaisampayana answers that the Pandavas governed with Dhritarashtra as their elder, consulting him, serving him with honour and giving him every comfort, while Bhima alone could not forget the dice match. The chapter sets the stage for the elders' later retirement to the forest.

scenes.B15C001S01: Janamejaya's question and Vaisampayana's account of how the Pandavas honoured Dhritarashtra as their ruling elder, with Bhima's lingering resentment.

shots.B15C001S01H01: Section heading naming the Asramavasa Parva.
shots.B15C001S01H02: Opening invocation, bowing to Narayana, Nara and Saraswati before the recital.
shots.B15C001S01H03: Janamejaya asks how the Pandavas behaved toward the old king and Gandhari after regaining the kingdom, and for how many years they ruled.
shots.B15C001S01H04: Vaisampayana says the Pandavas ruled under Dhritarashtra's guidance and waited on him and Gandhari with honour, supplied with comforts and gifts, while Vidura, Sanjaya, Yuyutsu, Kripa and Vyasa attended him; only Bhima could not let go of the dice match.

B15C002.summary: Vaisampayana describes how the Pandavas, led by Yudhishthira, kept honouring Dhritarashtra and Gandhari and carried out their wishes, including funeral offerings for the dead sons. Yudhishthira forgave old wrongs and would punish anyone who spoke against the old king, and Dhritarashtra came to trust him. Bhima, however, could only show respect outwardly, which hints at trouble to come.

scenes.B15C002S01: The Pandavas serve Dhritarashtra and Gandhari with care, and Yudhishthira's gentle conduct wins the old king's trust while Bhima stays reluctant.

shots.B15C002S01H01: The Pandavas honour the old king, who lives contentedly; Yudhishthira makes gifts on his behalf, the brothers follow his orders, and Gandhari makes offerings for her slain sons.
shots.B15C002S01H02: Dhritarashtra sees no ill-will in Yudhishthira and is pleased; Yudhishthira forgives old wrongs and punishes anyone who speaks against the king, while Bhima obeys only outwardly and grows cheerless.

B15C003.summary: Bhima's bitter outburst before Dhritarashtra and Gandhari deepens the old king's grief, and after fifteen years he admits his past folly and asks leave to retire to the forest with Gandhari. Yudhishthira is stricken, offers the throne to someone else and says he will follow the old king into the woods if he goes. When Dhritarashtra insists, Yudhishthira collapses into grief, and the old king is revived only by his touch, so the departure is delayed until the sage Vyasa arrives.

scenes.B15C003S01: Bhima's outburst, Dhritarashtra's confession and request to retire to the forest, and Yudhishthira's distressed reply.
scenes.B15C003S02: Dhritarashtra collapses, Yudhishthira's grief and touch revive him, and he asks again to eat and to leave, just as Vyasa arrives.

shots.B15C003S01H01: The Kurus see no change in Yudhishthira's warmth toward Dhritarashtra, but Bhima secretly defies him, then openly boasts before him and Gandhari that his arms killed the sons, which deeply saddens the old king; after fifteen years Dhritarashtra despairs, and he calls his friends to speak.
shots.B15C003S01H02: Dhritarashtra confesses he backed Duryodhana against the advice of Vasudeva, the wise men and Vyasa, regrets not giving the Pandavas their share, and describes his fasting, sleeping on grass and his and Gandhari's penances.
shots.B15C003S01H03: Dhritarashtra says the fallen sons have gone to a warrior's reward and asks leave to live in the forest with Gandhari, noting that a king shares in the merit and sin of his realm.
shots.B15C003S01H04: Yudhishthira says he cannot bear the old king's suffering, calls himself unworthy of the throne, offers it to Yuyutsu or anyone else, and vows to follow him if he goes to the forest.
shots.B15C003S01H05: Dhritarashtra says he has long been cared for and it is his family's custom to retire in old age, and asks Yudhishthira's permission.
shots.B15C003S02H01: Dhritarashtra asks Sanjaya and Kripa to speak for him, then leans on Gandhari and seems to lose consciousness, and Yudhishthira is filled with grief.
shots.B15C003S02H02: Yudhishthira laments that the strong king now leans on a woman, blames himself, and says he will fast if the old king and Gandhari do.
shots.B15C003S02H03: Yudhishthira bathes the old king's chest and face with cold water and touches him with his hand, and Dhritarashtra regains his senses.
shots.B15C003S02H04: Dhritarashtra asks to be touched and embraced again, says he is weak from missing his meal, and credits Yudhishthira's touch with restoring him.
shots.B15C003S02H05: Yudhishthira embraces the old king, the others weep, and Dhritarashtra again asks leave. Yudhishthira agrees to do what pleases him and asks him to eat; the old king agrees to eat with permission, and then Vyasa comes in.

B15C004.summary: Vyasa tells Yudhishthira not to stand in the way of the old king's retirement, since going to the forest in old age is the path royal sages take. Yudhishthira honours Vyasa as his father and teacher and accepts his advice. Vyasa then leaves, and Yudhishthira asks the old king to eat before he goes to his forest retreat.

scenes.B15C004S01: Vyasa urges Yudhishthira to let Dhritarashtra retire to the forest, and Yudhishthira agrees and asks him to eat first.

shots.B15C004S01H01: Vyasa tells Yudhishthira not to obstruct the old king, who is nearing the end of life, since retirement to the woods is what royal sages do.
shots.B15C004S01H02: Yudhishthira calls Vyasa his preceptor, father and the refuge of the kingdom and says a son must obey his father.
shots.B15C004S01H03: Vyasa agrees, recalls that Pandu revered the old king, notes that the Pandavas have served him faithfully, and says the old king bears no anger against them.
shots.B15C004S01H04: Vyasa soothes the old king, Yudhishthira says he agrees, Vyasa leaves for the forest, and Yudhishthira asks his father to eat before he goes to the forest retreat, promising to carry out the advice of the others.
shots.B15C004S01H05: Section heading marking the start of Section V.

B15C005.summary: Dhritarashtra returns to his palace with Gandhari, Vidura, Sanjaya and Kripa, and after the meal he calls Yudhishthira to his side. He then gives a long set of counsels on ruling a kingdom: honour the learned elders, choose loyal ministers, rely on well-tested spies, guard the city, the king's person and the royal household, punish offenders fairly, and keep a fixed daily routine. The chapter is the old king passing on his experience of statecraft to the new ruler.

scenes.B15C005S01: Dhritarashtra goes home, takes his meal, and then gives Yudhishthira detailed advice on governing.

shots.B15C005S01H01: Dhritarashtra goes home with Gandhari and his attendants, eats with Kunti and the others, and then tells Yudhishthira to rule his kingdom by heeding the elders, choosing trusted ministers, keeping spies, guarding his city and person, punishing offenders fairly, and keeping a daily routine.

B15C006.summary: Dhritarashtra goes on with his lessons in statecraft, explaining the circles of friends, enemies and neutral powers and the six policies of peace, war, marching, halting, sowing dissension and conciliation. He advises Yudhishthira when to fight and when to seek peace, how to give up land, wealth or troops in a way that costs least, and to protect the helpless. He ends by advising a weaker king to resist strong invaders and, if that fails, to fall fighting.

scenes.B15C006S01: Dhritarashtra explains the circles of allies and foes, the six policies, and how a king should act when stronger or weaker than his rival.

shots.B15C006S01H01: Dhritarashtra lists the circles of friends and foes, the six policies, the rules for making war or peace, the protection of the helpless, and the image of the cane, ending with advice that a hopeless defender should fall fighting.

B15C007.summary: Dhritarashtra tells Yudhishthira to weigh his own strength against an enemy's before going to war, and to march only when his troops are healthy and cheerful. He lists the kinds of power a king should gather, such as allies, wealth, forest tribes, paid soldiers, the trading classes and spies, and names some battle formations. He closes by saying Bhishma, Krishna and Vidura have already taught Yudhishthira these duties, and that a righteous king earns merit equal to that of a hundred horse-sacrifices.

scenes.B15C007S01: Dhritarashtra advises when to make war or peace, the kinds of power a king should keep, and how to prepare an army.

shots.B15C007S01H01: Dhritarashtra advises Yudhishthira to weigh war and peace carefully, to fight only when his side is strong and his foe weak, to gather several kinds of power, to prepare his army well, and to rule his subjects righteously, which he says earns great merit.

B15C008.summary: Yudhishthira agrees to follow his uncle's advice and asks him to keep teaching him, since Bhishma has gone to heaven and Krishna has gone to Dwaraka. Dhritarashtra then sends for Gandhari and tells her he will leave once Yudhishthira grants leave, but first he wants to make gifts in memory of his dead sons. He summons the people of the realm and the Brahmins, and tells them he means to retire to the forest.

scenes.B15C008S01: Yudhishthira agrees to the advice, Dhritarashtra plans his gifts and departure with Gandhari, and he tells the assembled people that he will retire to the forest.

shots.B15C008S01H01: Yudhishthira promises to follow the advice and asks for more teaching, noting that Bhishma has gone to heaven and the slayer of Madhu (Krishna) has left for Dwaraka, while Vidura and Sanjaya will go to the forest with the old king.
shots.B15C008S01H02: Dhritarashtra tells him to stop, since he has borne great toil, then goes to Gandhari's apartments, where she asks when he will leave with Yudhishthira's permission.
shots.B15C008S01H03: Dhritarashtra says he has the blessing of Vyasa, will leave once Yudhishthira agrees, and first wants to give away wealth in memory of his sons who were addicted to the dice, inviting the people to his house.
shots.B15C008S01H04: Yudhishthira brings what is needed, and Brahmins and people of all classes gather; Dhritarashtra tells them he has long lived with them, asks their leave to go to the forest, and they lament aloud in tears.

B15C009.summary: Dhritarashtra speaks to the assembled people, recalling how earlier rulers, including Santanu, Vichitraviryya and his brother Pandu, governed them well. He admits that his son's pride and his own poor judgment led to the great slaughter of royalty, asks forgiveness for himself and Gandhari, and entrusts Yudhishthira to their care. The citizens and countryfolk are moved to tears and say nothing, only looking at one another.

scenes.B15C009S01: Dhritarashtra asks the people's forgiveness, commends Yudhishthira to them, and they respond only in silent tears.

shots.B15C009S01H01: Dhritarashtra recalls the earlier kings, admits his own and Duryodhana's faults that led to the slaughter, asks the people to forgive him and Gandhari, commends Yudhishthira and his brothers to their care, and begs their pardon for his sons; the citizens weep and say nothing.

B15C010.summary: The citizens stand silent in grief until Dhritarashtra asks them again for permission to leave. A Brahmin named Samba answers on the assembly's behalf, approving the old king's departure, praising Yudhishthira's rule and absolving Duryodhana and Dhritarashtra of blame for the war, which he attributes to fate. The assembly approves, and the old king dismisses it and goes home with Gandhari.

scenes.B15C010S01: Dhritarashtra asks the citizens' leave, Samba speaks for them and blames fate for the war, and the old king dismisses the assembly.

shots.B15C010S01H01: Dhritarashtra, seeing the citizens too grief-stricken to speak, asks their leave again, saying he has the consent of his father the island-born Krishna (Vyasa) and of Yudhishthira.
shots.B15C010S01H02: The citizens weep, then choose the learned Brahmin Samba to reply, and he tells the old king that his rule was good and that Duryodhana never wronged them, praising Yudhishthira as well.
shots.B15C010S01H03: Samba says the destruction of the Kurus was caused by fate and could not be stopped, names the chief warriors who fell, and asks the king to absolve his son and to trust the Pandavas to rule well.
shots.B15C010S01H04: The assembly approves, the old king thanks the people and sends them away, and he returns to his mansion with Gandhari.

B15C011.summary: The next day Dhritarashtra sends Vidura to Yudhishthira, asking for wealth to hold funeral offerings for Bhishma, Drona, Somadatta, Valhika, his sons and Jayadratha, and announcing that he will leave on the Kartika full moon. Yudhishthira and Arjuna welcome the request, but Bhima angrily objects, recalling the dice match and the hardships of exile. Arjuna urges him to accept, and Yudhishthira silences Bhima when his anger threatens to say more.

scenes.B15C011S01: Vidura brings Dhritarashtra's request for funeral wealth, Yudhishthira and Arjuna accept, and Bhima's angry objection is silenced.

shots.B15C011S01H01: Vidura reports Dhritarashtra's plan to leave on the Kartika full moon and asks for wealth for the funeral offerings; Yudhishthira and Arjuna agree, Bhima objects bitterly, Arjuna urges him to yield, and Yudhishthira tells him to be silent.

B15C012.summary: Arjuna tells Bhima that Dhritarashtra deserves honour and that good men forget the wrongs done to them. Yudhishthira then tells Vidura to say to the old king that he may take as much wealth from the royal treasury as he wishes, and that Bhima should not be made unhappy. Yudhishthira also offers the king everything he and Arjuna own, to show his goodwill.

scenes.B15C012S01: Arjuna urges Bhima to honour the old king, and Yudhishthira offers Dhritarashtra wealth from the treasury and from the brothers' houses.

shots.B15C012S01H01: Arjuna tells his elder brother Bhima that they should honour Dhritarashtra and forget old wrongs, and Yudhishthira tells Vidura to say that the old king may take as much wealth from the treasury as he wants for the funeral gifts, and asks that Bhima not be made unhappy.
shots.B15C012S01H02: Yudhishthira praises Arjuna, Bhima glares at Arjuna, and Yudhishthira says Dhritarashtra may take what he likes from his and Arjuna's houses and that his own body is at the king's disposal.

B15C013.summary: Vidura returns and reports to Dhritarashtra that Yudhishthira and Arjuna agree to his plan, and that Bhima accepted only reluctantly. Yudhishthira offers his kingdom, his life and all his wealth, and asks the king to forgive Bhima's outburst. The brothers also suggest charitable gifts to Brahmins, the poor and the blind, along with pavilions of food and water for cattle, and Dhritarashtra resolves to hold the great gift-giving on the Kartika full moon.

scenes.B15C013S01: Vidura reports Yudhishthira's and Arjuna's consent, Bhima's reluctant acceptance and the charities proposed, and Dhritarashtra resolves to proceed.

shots.B15C013S01H01: Vidura reports to Dhritarashtra the brothers' offers of wealth and service, Bhima's reluctant consent, and the charitable gifts they suggest; Dhritarashtra is pleased and resolves to make large gifts on the Kartika full moon.

B15C014.summary: Pleased with the Pandavas, Dhritarashtra invites many Brahmins and sages and gives away wealth for the spirits of Bhishma, his sons, friends and kinsmen, naming each recipient as the gifts go out. Yudhishthira approves, and the gifts are lavish in cars, clothes, gold, livestock, slaves, elephants and horses, along with food and drink, music and dancing. The text says the ten-day gift-giving frees the old king from the debts he owed his sons and grandsons.

scenes.B15C014S01: Dhritarashtra makes lavish gifts and feeds the guests for ten days, in memory of the dead, with Yudhishthira's approval.

shots.B15C014S01H01: Dhritarashtra invites thousands of Brahmins and sages and gives away vast quantities of goods, animals and maidens, naming each dead kinsman in turn; Yudhishthira approves, the gifts are multiplied for the recipients, food and entertainment follow, and after ten days the old king feels freed from his debts to his sons and grandsons.

B15C015.summary: On the Kartika full moon Dhritarashtra completes the final rites, takes the sacred fire, puts on deer-skin and bark, and leaves his palace with Gandhari, Kunti and his daughters-in-law. Yudhishthira faints in grief and the Pandavas, Vidura, Sanjaya, Kripa and Dhaumya follow, while the women and citizens lament as they once did when the Pandavas were exiled after the dice match. The chapter closes the palace phase of the old king's life and begins his journey to the forest.

scenes.B15C015S01: Dhritarashtra leaves the palace for the forest, Yudhishthira collapses in grief, and the whole city follows in lamentation.

shots.B15C015S01H01: Dhritarashtra completes the rites on the Kartika full moon, dresses in deer-skin and bark, and leaves with Gandhari, Kunti and the others while Yudhishthira faints and the Pandavas, Vidura, Sanjaya, Kripa and Dhaumya follow, and the citizens lament.

B15C016.summary: Dhritarashtra leaves the city amid a great crowd and sends the citizens home, keeping Vidura and Sanjaya with him but handing Kripa and Yuyutsu back to Yudhishthira. Yudhishthira tries to hold his mother Kunti back, and she answers with a speech of regret and farewell, recalling Karna and asking the brothers to care for their wives and one another. Yudhishthira, Bhima and the others plead with her in vain, and she goes on with Gandhari toward the forest.

scenes.B15C016S01: Dhritarashtra leaves the city, Yudhishthira is left behind, and Kunti refuses all pleas to turn back and follows Gandhari into the forest.

shots.B15C016S01H01: The old king leaves the city through a crowded street, bids the people go home, keeps Vidura and Sanjaya with him, hands Kripa and Yuyutsu over to Yudhishthira, and Kunti refuses her son's request to return and keeps holding Gandhari as they go.
shots.B15C016S01H02: Kunti asks Yudhishthira to care for Sahadeva, Draupadi and the other brothers, confesses that she never revealed Karna's birth as the son of Surya, and says she will live in the forest with Gandhari, serving her in-laws.
shots.B15C016S01H03: Yudhishthira refuses to let her go and reminds her of Vidula's words and of the wisdom she once gave them through Vasudeva, Bhima pleads with her too, but Kunti ignores them; Draupadi and Subhadra follow weeping, and Kunti then speaks to her children.

B15C017.summary: Kunti explains that she spurred her sons to courage after the loss at dice, so they would not be disgraced or lose their fame, and that she acted to protect Draupadi from Dussasana's insults. She tells them that she does not want the kingdom they won and will spend her days in penance and service to her in-laws. She asks Yudhishthira and his brothers to stop following her and to keep to righteousness.

scenes.B15C017S01: Kunti explains why she roused her sons, declines any share of the kingdom, and tells them to go back.

shots.B15C017S01H01: Kunti says she urged her sons to courage after the dice loss to keep their fame and to avenge Draupadi's humiliation, that she has no wish for the kingdom they won, and that she will do penance, so they should stop following her and keep to righteousness.

B15C018.summary: The Pandavas are ashamed and turn back, and Dhritarashtra asks Gandhari to make Kunti return, but Kunti will not be moved. The Kuru ladies wail, the Pandavas go back to a mourning city, and the old king's party camps by the Bhagirathi, where they perform their rites and rest for the night. Their first day in the forest is painful, both for them and for the grieving people they have left behind.

scenes.B15C018S01: The Pandavas turn back, Kunti stays, and the old king's party camps by the Bhagirathi for the night, with the city left in mourning.

shots.B15C018S01H01: The Pandavas, ashamed, stop following Kunti, who will not return despite Dhritarashtra's appeal through Gandhari; the Pandavas go back to a city in mourning, while Dhritarashtra's party camps on the banks of the Bhagirathi, performs its rites and sleeps, then sets out again the next morning.

B15C019.summary: Following Vidura's advice, Dhritarashtra settles on the banks of the Bhagirathi, where visiting Brahmins and common folk see him, and then moves to Kurukshetra. There the former Kekaya king Satayupa welcomes him and takes him to Vyasa, who initiates him into the forest way of life. Dhritarashtra, Gandhari, Kunti, Vidura and Sanjaya then take up barks and skins and practise severe penance.

scenes.B15C019S01: Dhritarashtra settles by the Bhagirathi, moves to Kurukshetra under Satayupa, is initiated by Vyasa, and his household takes up severe penance.

shots.B15C019S01H01: Following Vidura's advice, Dhritarashtra makes his home on the Bhagirathi, meets visitors, bathes, moves to Kurukshetra and Satayupa's hermitage, is initiated into the forest life by Vyasa, and his household, including Gandhari, Kunti, Vidura and Sanjaya, takes up barks, skins and severe austerities.

B15C020.summary: The sages Narada, Parvata, Devala and Vyasa visit the old king and gladden him with talk of religion. Narada tells of earlier royal ascetics who reached heaven through penance in the forest, and says Dhritarashtra and Gandhari will reach a high goal, with Vidura and Sanjaya also going on. Asked by Satayupa for the particulars, Narada says he has heard from Indra that Dhritarashtra has three years of life left, after which he will go to Kuvera's realm, and the company departs well pleased.

scenes.B15C020S01: The sages visit Dhritarashtra, Narada tells of the forest-penance heroes and foretells the old king's end, and the assembly leaves in good spirits.

shots.B15C020S01H01: Narada, Parvata, Devala, Vyasa and the royal sage Satayupa come to see Dhritarashtra, Kunti serves them, and they speak to the old king on religion and righteousness until Narada speaks up.
shots.B15C020S01H02: Narada recounts several earlier kings, from Sahasrachitya to Sasaloman, who won heaven by penance in the forest, and says Dhritarashtra and Gandhari will do the same, Pandu watches over them, Vidura will enter Yudhishthira, and Sanjaya will rise to heaven through meditation.
shots.B15C020S01H03: The assembly praises Narada and honours him, and Satayupa asks him what final region Dhritarashtra will reach and when.
shots.B15C020S01H04: Narada says that in Indra's abode he heard that Dhritarashtra has three years of life left, after which he will go to Kuvera's realm, and that the question is a secret of the gods.
shots.B15C020S01H05: Dhritarashtra and the others are cheered by Narada's words, and the company leaves by the path of those who have attained success.

B15C021.summary: With the elders gone to the forest, the Pandavas and the citizens of Hastinapura grieve, worrying how the old king, Gandhari, Kunti, Vidura and Sanjaya will manage in the wilds. The Pandavas lose interest in rule and in study, dwelling on the deaths of Abhimanyu, Karna and Draupadi's sons. They are only partly comforted by the survival of Parikshit, the son of Virata's daughter.

scenes.B15C021S01: The Brahmins and citizens fret over the elders in the forest, the Pandavas grieve for their losses, and Parikshit gives them some comfort.

shots.B15C021S01H01: The Brahmins and citizens wonder how the old king, Gandhari, Kunti, Vidura and Sanjaya will fare in the forest, the Pandavas have no joy in rule, study or women, grieve for Abhimanyu, Karna and the other dead, and are only kept going by the survival of Parikshit.

B15C022.summary: The Pandavas, lost in grief, neglect the affairs of the capital and think constantly of their mother and the blind old couple in the forest. Sahadeva proposes going to see them, and Draupadi agrees and asks for the visit. Yudhishthira orders the army, carts, treasuries and kitchens made ready, and after waiting five days for citizens who wish to come, he sets out for the forest.

scenes.B15C022S01: The Pandavas, grieving, resolve to visit the forest, and Yudhishthira orders the army and supplies prepared for the journey.

shots.B15C022S01H01: The Pandavas, grieving and neglecting their duties, worry about Kunti and the old couple, Sahadeva and Draupadi urge a visit, Yudhishthira orders the army, carts, kitchens and pavilions readied, and after five days of waiting for citizens he sets out.

B15C023.summary: The Pandavas set out with a great procession of troops, chariots, elephants, camels and litter-borne women, with Yudhishthira under a white umbrella and his brothers and Draupadi around him. Kripa leads the army ahead toward the retreat, while Yuyutsu and Dhaumya stay behind to guard the city. Crossing the Yamuna, Yudhishthira sees the old king's hermitage in the distance, and the crowd rushes in with joy.

scenes.B15C023S01: The great procession sets out, with each Pandava described in his conveyance, and Yudhishthira catches sight of the old king's hermitage across the Yamuna.

shots.B15C023S01H01: The army marches out with Kripa in command, Yudhishthira rides in state with Brahmins and bards, Bhima on an elephant, the twins on horses, Arjuna on a chariot, Draupadi and the women in litters, Yuyutsu and Dhaumya guard the city, and after crossing the Yamuna the whole crowd sees the hermitage and enters the forest in high spirits.

B15C024.summary: The Pandavas walk the last stretch on foot in humility, and the hermit community tells them the old king has gone to bathe in the Yamuna. Sahadeva runs ahead to Kunti, who rushes toward the blind couple, and the brothers fall to the ground before their father. Dhritarashtra recognises them by voice and touch, and Yudhishthira introduces the women and people of the court to him. The old king feels as if he is back in Hastinapura, and he returns to his forest hermitage with a crowd of visitors.

scenes.B15C024S01: The Pandavas reach the hermitage on foot, reunite with Dhritarashtra, Gandhari and Kunti, and present the court to the old king.

shots.B15C024S01H01: The Pandavas walk to the hermitage on foot, learn from ascetics that the old king is at the Yamuna, Sahadeva runs to Kunti, who hurries ahead of the old couple, the brothers fall to the ground in greeting, the king recognises them by voice and touch, and Yudhishthira presents the whole court to him.

B15C025.summary: The visiting ascetics ask which of the newcomers is Yudhishthira, Bhima, Arjuna, the twins and Draupadi, and Sanjaya names each of them by their looks. He then names the other women of the household, including Subhadra, Ulupi, Chitrangada, Jarasandha's daughter, Virata's daughter who was Abhimanyu's wife, and the widows of Dhritarashtra's sons, who are dressed in white. Afterwards the old king makes courteous enquiries of the whole company.

scenes.B15C025S01: The ascetics ask who is who, Sanjaya points out and describes each Pandava and wife, and the old king greets the company.

shots.B15C025S01H01: The Pandavas sit with the old king in his hermitage, and visiting ascetics ask who each of them is, along with Draupadi and the other ladies of the household.
shots.B15C025S01H02: Sanjaya describes Yudhishthira, Bhima, Arjuna, the twins, Kunti's daughters-in-law and the widows, pointing out Krishna (Draupadi), Subhadra, Ulupi, Chitrangada, the wives of Bhima and the twins, Virata's daughter who was Abhimanyu's wife, and the widows of Dhritarashtra's sons.
shots.B15C025S01H03: After the ascetics leave, the old king sits with the Pandavas and the women and children, and makes the usual polite enquiries.

B15C026.summary: Dhritarashtra asks Yudhishthira a long series of questions about his kingdom, justice, treasury, priests and ministers, and the duties of his subjects. Yudhishthira asks after the old king's peace and his mother's welfare, and then wonders where Vidura is. Vidura appears, emaciated and naked, and Yudhishthira chases him into the forest. Vidura enters Yudhishthira's body by Yoga and dies, and a voice tells Yudhishthira not to cremate the body, since Vidura was Dharma and goes to a heavenly region. The brothers are fed by the old king and sleep under a tree.

scenes.B15C026S01: Dhritarashtra and Yudhishthira exchange questions, then Vidura appears and passes into Yudhishthira's body, and his own body is not to be cremated.

shots.B15C026S01H01: Dhritarashtra asks Yudhishthira a long series of questions about his welfare, his household, his kingdom, the Brahmins, the women, and whether the Kuru race has kept its fame.
shots.B15C026S01H02: Yudhishthira is ready to answer and begins by asking after the old king in turn.
shots.B15C026S01H03: Yudhishthira asks whether the old king's penance is going well, whether Kunti can serve him without fatigue and whether she still grieves for her sons and blames the brothers, and asks where Vidura and Sanjaya are.
shots.B15C026S01H04: Dhritarashtra says Vidura lives on air and is seen in the forest, Vidura then appears emaciated and naked, runs from Yudhishthira, stops, and enters Yudhishthira's body by Yoga, leaving his own body dead; a voice tells Yudhishthira not to burn it, since Vidura was Dharma and goes to the Santanika regions, and Dhritarashtra then offers the brothers fruits and roots, which they eat before sleeping under a tree.

B15C027.summary: The Pandavas spend the night on the bare ground beside their mother and eat the food of the hermitage. The next morning Yudhishthira tours the surrounding retreats with his brothers, giving gifts to the ascetics, and then returns to his uncle, who is seated with Gandhari. Satayupa and the other sages of Kurukshetra arrive, followed by Vyasa, who is given an honoured seat and bids the assembly be seated.

scenes.B15C027S01: The Pandavas spend the night in the hermitage, tour the sacred retreats, and gather round the old king for the arrival of Vyasa.

shots.B15C027S01H01: The Pandavas spend the night on the ground beside their mother, Yudhishthira tours the hermitages with his brothers and gives gifts to the ascetics, returns to Dhritarashtra, who welcomes the brothers and Kunti, and Satayupa and the others arrive, followed by Vyasa, who takes an honoured seat as the assembly sits down.

B15C028.summary: Once the Pandavas are seated, Vyasa asks Dhritarashtra how his penances are going and whether his grief has eased, and asks after Gandhari, Kunti and the brothers. He then explains that Vidura was Dharma himself, born through a curse and Vyasa's own power, and that Yudhishthira is also a son of Dharma, and that Vidura has entered Yudhishthira's person. Vyasa offers to show the old king some wonder, and asks what he wants to see or hear.

scenes.B15C028S01: Vyasa asks after the family's welfare, explains the divine parentage of Vidura and Yudhishthira, and offers to grant a wish.

shots.B15C028S01H01: Vyasa asks Dhritarashtra about his penances and grief, asks after Gandhari, Kunti and the Pandavas, explains that Vidura was Dharma born by a curse and Vyasa's own power and that Yudhishthira is also Dharma's son, and offers to show a wonder or grant any wish.

B15C029.summary: Janamejaya asks what wonder Vyasa performed, and how long the Pandavas stayed in the forest and what they ate. Vaisampayana says they lived there about a month on the food they could find, and that sages gathered round, including Narada, Parvata and Devala. Vyasa offers Dhritarashtra any boon, and the old king speaks at length of his grief for his sons and his fear for his own end. Gandhari, whose grief is renewed, asks Vyasa to let the dead be seen, and Vyasa then turns to Kunti to ask what is on her mind.

scenes.B15C029S01: Janamejaya asks his questions, Vyasa offers a boon, Dhritarashtra laments his sons, Gandhari asks for a sight of the dead, and Kunti prepares to speak.

shots.B15C029S01H01: Section heading naming the Putradarsana Parva, the Parva of the sight of sons.
shots.B15C029S01H02: Janamejaya asks Vaisampayana what wonder Vyasa worked, how many days the Pandavas stayed in the forest, and what food they lived on.
shots.B15C029S01H03: The Pandavas live a month in the forest, sages come and talk with them, and Vyasa offers the old king any boon; Dhritarashtra, grieving for his sons and their ruin, says he has no peace of mind.
shots.B15C029S01H04: Gandhari, Kunti, Draupadi and Subhadra grieve afresh; Gandhari begs Vyasa to let the king see his children; Vyasa asks Kunti what is on her mind, and she prepares to tell him something from the past.

B15C030.summary: Kunti confesses to Vyasa the secret of Karna's birth. As a girl she had served the wrathful sage Durvasas, who gave her a mantra, and she summoned the sun god, who fathered Karna and restored her maidenhood. Fearing shame to her father, she set the infant adrift in water and never acknowledged him, and she asks Vyasa to grant her wish to see her son, and the king his. Vyasa tells her she is blameless, since gods can beget children in several ways.

scenes.B15C030S01: Kunti tells Vyasa how she came to bear Karna, and Vyasa absolves her and promises to grant her wish.

shots.B15C030S01H01: Kunti tells Vyasa that the sage Durvasas gave her a mantra, that she summoned the sun god, who fathered Karna and restored her virginity, and that she set the child in the water and never acknowledged him; she asks Vyasa to let her see her son and the king his wish. Vyasa tells her she is blameless, since gods can beget children by thought, sight or touch.

B15C031.summary: Vyasa promises that the king, Gandhari and Kunti will see their dead that night, and explains that the fallen heroes were portions of gods, celestial beings and sages who came to earth for a purpose and have now returned. He names several of them, including Dhritarashtra as the Gandharva king, Pandu as one of the Maruts, Yudhishthira and Vidura as Dharma, Duryodhana as Kali and Karna as a portion of the sun. He tells the company to go to the Bhagirathi, where they will see the dead, and they set out with joy.

scenes.B15C031S01: Vyasa tells the women they will see their dead and explains the divine origins of the heroes, and the company goes to the Bhagirathi to wait for night.

shots.B15C031S01H01: Vyasa promises Gandhari, Kunti and Draupadi that they will see their dead, explains that the heroes were portions of divine beings who came down to earth for a purpose, names several of them, and tells everyone to go to the Bhagirathi.
shots.B15C031S01H02: The whole company, including Dhritarashtra and the Pandavas, goes to the Bhagirathi, takes up camp on the bank, and waits out the day until night falls.

B15C032.summary: At night the company gathers by the Bhagirathi and Vyasa bathes in its waters and calls up the dead. Warriors from both sides rise from the river in celestial robes and jewels, free of anger and pride, and Gandhari sees her sons and others with divine sight that Vyasa grants. Dhritarashtra also receives the sight, and the whole scene looks like a festival, and he is filled with joy at seeing the heroes.

scenes.B15C032S01: Vyasa calls the dead from the Bhagirathi, the warriors of both sides rise, and Dhritarashtra and Gandhari see them with the sight Vyasa gives.

shots.B15C032S01H01: After the evening rites, the company gathers and Vyasa calls up the dead from the Bhagirathi, Bhishma, Drona, Karna, Duryodhana and the other warriors of both sides rise in celestial robes, Gandhari and Dhritarashtra receive divine sight, and the old king is full of joy.

B15C033.summary: The reunited dead and living meet with joy, and the Pandavas are reconciled with Karna, so that old enmities are set aside for one night. Vyasa then dismisses the crowd, the warriors go off to their heavenly realms, and the widows enter the Bhagirathi to join their husbands. The chapter ends with Vyasa's promise of rewards for those who hear or recite this account.

scenes.B15C033S01: The living and the dead are reconciled and then dismissed, the widows join their husbands, and the chapter closes with praise for hearing the story.

shots.B15C033S01H01: Sons, wives, brothers and friends meet the dead, the Pandavas are reconciled with Karna, and everyone spends the night in happiness; then Vyasa dismisses the crowd, the dead return to their heavenly realms, the widows bathe in the river to join their husbands, and the text ends with rewards promised to those who hear or recite this narrative.

B15C034.summary: Janamejaya asks how bodies that have been destroyed can appear again in the same form, and Vaisampayana answers with a long philosophical reply. He says deeds are never lost without their consequences, that the body arises from deeds while the soul is unaffected by pleasure and pain, and that the sorrow of separation comes from confusing the body with the self. The discourse makes the apparition a matter of how the soul and deeds persist.

scenes.B15C034S01: Janamejaya asks how the dead can reappear, and Vaisampayana answers with a discourse on deeds, the soul and the body.

shots.B15C034S01H01: Sauti says Janamejaya was pleased with the story and asks Vaisampayana how dead bodies can return in their old forms.
shots.B15C034S01H02: Vaisampayana says deeds are never lost, the body is born from deeds, the soul is not harmed by pleasure or pain, grief over separation is foolish, and only knowing body from self frees a person from error.

B15C035.summary: Dhritarashtra, who had never seen his sons, gains sight through Vyasa's grace and sees them as they were. Janamejaya asks to see his own father in the same form, and Vyasa brings Parikshit back from the other world, along with Samika and Sringin. Astika, a learned Brahmin, praises the sacrifice and the wondrous history, and Janamejaya asks Vaisampayana what followed for Dhritarashtra in the forest.

scenes.B15C035S01: Dhritarashtra gains sight, Janamejaya sees his father Parikshit brought back, Astika speaks in praise, and Janamejaya asks for the sequel.

shots.B15C035S01H01: Vaisampayana says Dhritarashtra, who had never seen his sons, now sees them through Vyasa's grace, and that Vidura and Dhritarashtra both attained success through their penances and Vyasa.
shots.B15C035S01H02: Janamejaya asks that Vyasa also show him his father as he was when he died, so that he may believe the story.
shots.B15C035S01H03: Sauti says Vyasa brings Parikshit back to life in his former form, along with Samika and Sringin, and Janamejaya bathes and pours water on his father, then speaks to Astika about the wonder of the sacrifice.
shots.B15C035S01H04: Astika says the sacrifice where Vyasa is present will conquer both worlds, recalls the destruction of the snakes and Takshaka's escape, and says the king has gained merit from seeing this history.
shots.B15C035S01H05: Sauti says Janamejaya honours Vaisampayana and asks him for the sequel to Dhritarashtra's life in the forest.

B15C036.summary: Janamejaya asks what Dhritarashtra and Yudhishthira did after the vision. Vyasa tells Dhritarashtra that the Pandavas should return to Hastinapura to rule, since more than a month has passed. Dhritarashtra agrees and, though Yudhishthira begs to stay and Gandhari insists he go, the brothers and women take their leave, and Yudhishthira sets out for the capital.

scenes.B15C036S01: The old king dismisses Yudhishthira and his household to return to the capital, after Yudhishthira's and Gandhari's protests and Kunti's farewell.

shots.B15C036S01H01: Janamejaya asks what Dhritarashtra and Yudhishthira did after seeing the dead.
shots.B15C036S01H02: Dhritarashtra is comforted, the crowd leaves, and Vyasa urges Dhritarashtra to send Yudhishthira back to rule, since more than a month has passed, and Dhritarashtra tells Yudhishthira he is content and has no need of him.
shots.B15C036S01H03: Yudhishthira says he has done nothing wrong and will serve the old couple, but Gandhari insists he return to the throne and obey his father.
shots.B15C036S01H04: Yudhishthira laments that the old king casts him off, names the ruined peoples, and says he wants only penance; Sahadeva says he will stay with his mothers, and Kunti sends all of them back home.
shots.B15C036S01H05: Yudhishthira agrees to go, Dhritarashtra blesses and dismisses the brothers, the women take their leave, and the party sets off for Hastinapura.

B15C037.summary: Two years after the Pandavas return to Hastinapura, the sage Narada visits Yudhishthira and asks about his father's fate. Narada reports that Dhritarashtra, with Gandhari, Kunti and Sanjaya, went to the Ganga and lived by severe penance, reduced to skin and bones. When a forest fire spread, Sanjaya urged escape, but the old king sat in meditation with the two queens and all three were burned, which the sage later confirmed from the bodies. The narrative thus reports the old king's death by fire, which the Pandavas then mourn.

scenes.B15C037S01: Narada visits Yudhishthira, who asks about his father, and Narada describes the old king's penance and death in a forest fire.
scenes.B15C037S02: The Pandavas, the palace and the citizens hear of the death and weep, and Yudhishthira speaks after his cries.

shots.B15C037S01H01: Section heading naming the Naradagamana Parva, the Parva of Narada's coming.
shots.B15C037S01H02: Two years after the return, Narada visits Yudhishthira, who welcomes him and asks about his health and the lands he has passed through.
shots.B15C037S01H03: Narada says he has not seen Yudhishthira for a long time and has come from his hermitage after visiting many sacred waters, including the Ganga.
shots.B15C037S01H04: Yudhishthira asks whether Narada has seen his father on the Ganga and asks after the health of the king, Gandhari, Kunti and Sanjaya.
shots.B15C037S01H05: Narada says the old king went to Gangadvara with his fire, Gandhari, Kunti and Sanjaya, lived on air and pebbles in severe penance, and finally sat in meditation as a forest fire burned him, Gandhari and Kunti; Sanjaya escaped to the Himalayas, and the ascetics did not mourn.
shots.B15C037S02H01: Hearing of the death, the Pandavas, the women of the palace and the citizens wail; Yudhishthira cries out in grief, then steadies himself and begins to speak.

B15C038.summary: Yudhishthira laments the death of his father in the forest fire, reflecting that fate is hard to predict for even a powerful king with a hundred sons. He mourns Kunti most, calls the fire-god ungrateful for burning the mother of Arjuna, whom he had once served at Khandava, and wishes that Bhima or Sahadeva had saved her. The sorrow of the brothers and the household is so great that the wails fill the palace and seem to reach the sky.

scenes.B15C038S01: Yudhishthira mourns his father, Gandhari and especially Kunti, blames the fire and his own brothers, and the household wails in grief.

shots.B15C038S01H01: Yudhishthira laments that fate is unpredictable, recalls his father's former splendour, grieves most for Kunti, blames the fire-god and Sahadeva, imagines her last cries, and the Pandavas and household weep as the cries fill the palace.

B15C039.summary: Narada corrects the account: Dhritarashtra did not die in an unsanctified fire but in his own sacred fire, which the attending priests had abandoned in the forest and which spread into a blaze. Yudhishthira and the whole household then perform the water offerings and cremation rites, and on the twelfth day make lavish gifts in memory of the old king and his queens. The section closes with a benediction on hearing the Asramavasika Parva, followed by the translator's notes on the text.

scenes.B15C039S01: Narada explains the cause of Dhritarashtra's death, Yudhishthira performs the funeral rites and gifts, and the parva closes with a benediction.
scenes.B15C039S02: Translator's notes 1 to 5, on the Aralikas, the Krishna incarnation, mahadana gifts, a variant reading, and the king's share of merit and demerit.
scenes.B15C039S03: Translator's notes 6 to 10, on royal armlets, the limbs of a kingdom, the open ground for soldiers, spies in grass, and corrupt officials.
scenes.B15C039S04: Translator's notes 11 to 15, on the wages of workers, the mandala circles, the four kinds of foes, the sixty items of policy, and good land and men.
scenes.B15C039S05: Translator's notes 16 to 20, on the reading of a compound, the image of the cane, the two kinds of war and peace, and the three kinds of strength.
scenes.B15C039S06: Translator's notes 21 to 25, on the forms of strength, the army types, the array formations, and the attack on the enemy's home ground.
scenes.B15C039S07: Translator's notes 26 to 30, on the state of the dead, textual corrections, Jayadratha's role, and modern gift customs.
scenes.B15C039S08: Translator's notes 31 to 35, on the multiplied gifts, Gandhari's bandage, the family ties of Kunti, dependence, and the demerit of receiving gifts.
scenes.B15C039S09: Translator's notes 36 to 40, on Kunti's words, the Brahmi night, the iron tiger-claws, a comparison of names, and Ulupi.
scenes.B15C039S10: Translator's notes 41 to 45, on the unfairness of a car attacking one on foot, Vidura's union with Yudhishthira, the peacock, ritual vessels, and the curse of Mandavya.
scenes.B15C039S11: Translator's notes 46 to 50, on the stages of Yoga, Valhika's family, the powers of the yogin, the incarnated gods, and the religion of withdrawal.
scenes.B15C039S12: Translator's notes 51 to 55, on the soul as a mirror, the wise man's self, the dissolution of the body, the sacrifice of animals, and avoidance of sorrow.
scenes.B15C039S13: Translator's notes 56 to 59, on knowledge of body and self, the unmanifest, the fate of deeds, a disclaimer on the translation, and a corrected reading.
scenes.B15C039S14: Translator's notes 60 to 62, on a grammar point, the meaning of emaciation, and a verb construction, then the book title lines.
scenes.B15C039S15: The author attribution line for the Mahabharata.

shots.B15C039S01H01: Narada says the old king was not burned by a profane fire, but by his own sacred fire, which the attending priests left in the forest and which spread into a blaze, and that Gandhari and Kunti have also attained a good end, so Yudhishthira should perform the water rites with his brothers.
shots.B15C039S01H02: The Pandavas, the household and the citizens go to the Ganga, make water offerings to the three, send men to Gangadvara for the cremation, and on the twelfth day give lavish gifts in memory of the old king and queens, after which Narada comforts Yudhishthira and departs, and Dhritarashtra's life is summed up as three years in the forest and fifteen in the city.
shots.B15C039S01H03: The closing benediction says that whoever listens to this Asramavasika Parva with attention and then feeds Brahmins with offerings will be rewarded.
shots.B15C039S01H04: Heading marking the end of the Asramavasika Parva.
shots.B15C039S01H05: Heading that introduces the translator's footnotes.
shots.B15C039S02H01: Note 1 explains the word Aralikas as cooks who prepared herbs cut with a blade, and describes the spiced preparation called Ragakhandava.
shots.B15C039S02H02: Note 2 recounts how the burdened earth asked the Grandsire for relief, and Vishnu incarnated as Krishna to lighten her load.
shots.B15C039S02H03: Note 3 explains that mahadana means large gifts such as elephants, boats, cars and horses, which can cause a Brahmin to lose his status if he accepts them.
shots.B15C039S02H04: Note 4 says a Bengal manuscript reads a different word here, with the same sense.
shots.B15C039S02H05: Note 5 explains that the king receives a sixth of the merit from sages under his protection and shares in the sins committed in his realm, because he failed to supervise them.
shots.B15C039S03H01: Note 6 says kings wore jewels and healing herbs in gold capsules on their arms, believed to guard against many evils.
shots.B15C039S03H02: Note 7 lists the eight limbs of a kingdom: law, judge, assessors, scribe, astrologer, gold, fire and water.
shots.B15C039S03H03: Note 8 explains atta as the open space kept for soldiers to tread on.
shots.B15C039S03H04: Note 9 says grass and darkness can hide the spies of an enemy.
shots.B15C039S03H05: Note 10 explains that the euphemistic term for corrupt officials and thieves, and the term for rash doers, correspond to culpable homicide in modern law.
shots.B15C039S04H01: Note 11 says workers should be content with their food and wages no higher than what feeds them.
shots.B15C039S04H02: Note 12 explains mandala and distinguishes neutrals from those who have equal feelings toward both sides.
shots.B15C039S04H03: Note 13 lists four kinds of foes and the six kinds of aggressors, including arsonists, poisoners and thieves.
shots.B15C039S04H04: Note 14 breaks down the sixty items into groups of eight, twenty-eight, fourteen and eighteen.
shots.B15C039S04H05: Note 15 explains the three qualities the text asks for: fertile land, pure gold and strong men.
shots.B15C039S05H01: Note 16 says the words Kasyanchidapadi should be read with the lines that follow.
shots.B15C039S05H02: Note 17 explains the image of the cane, which yields to pressure, and retells a tale from the Santi Parva about the Ocean and the rivers.
shots.B15C039S05H03: Note 18 explains that war and peace each come in two forms, depending on whether the enemy is strong or weak, and corrects variant readings.
shots.B15C039S05H04: Note 19 says the verse is expanded a little, following the commentator.
shots.B15C039S05H05: Note 20 says strength comes in three kinds, explained in the next verse.
shots.B15C039S06H01: Note 21 explains readiness of the forces, the king's control over them, and strength of counsels.
shots.B15C039S06H02: Note 22 explains the strength of money, forest irregulars, the paid standing army, and the artisans and traders who supported it.
shots.B15C039S06H03: Note 23 describes the Sakata, Padma and Vajra battle arrays.
shots.B15C039S06H04: Note 24 explains that the king should meet the enemy either inside his own land or by invading the enemy's land.
shots.B15C039S06H05: Note 25 says the phrase means winning fame here and felicity hereafter.
shots.B15C039S07H01: Note 26 explains that the dead first become Pretas for a year, until the Sapindikarana rite, after which they join the Pitris, and that gifts help them on the way.
shots.B15C039S07H02: Note 27 says the verse that mentions thousands of years for Yudhishthira's rule is probably corrupt.
shots.B15C039S07H03: Note 28 gives the correct reading as jane, not kshane.
shots.B15C039S07H04: Note 29 argues that Jayadratha's wrongs to the Pandavas were smaller than Duryodhana's, since he played a minor part in Abhimanyu's death and only tried to abduct Draupadi.
shots.B15C039S07H05: Note 30 says modern Sraddha and wedding gifts follow much the same pattern, with mantras said over heaped gifts and names called out by a superintendent.
shots.B15C039S08H01: Note 31 says each gift Dhritarashtra named was multiplied tenfold at Yudhishthira's command.
shots.B15C039S08H02: Note 32 explains that Gandhari kept her eyes bandaged from marriage, out of devotion to her blind husband.
shots.B15C039S08H03: Note 33 explains Kunti's regard for Dhritarashtra as a father, which makes Gandhari her mother-in-law, since the eldest brother counts as a father.
shots.B15C039S08H04: Note 34 explains that living by the faces of others means living in dependence on them.
shots.B15C039S08H05: Note 35 says mahadana gifts bring merit to the giver but demerit to the receiver unless he is exceptional, and that accepting them still marks a man as fallen.
shots.B15C039S09H01: Note 36 says Kunti's words were just and her sons' opposition unreasonable, which is why they felt shame.
shots.B15C039S09H02: Note 37 explains that a Brahmi night is one spent singing sacred hymns.
shots.B15C039S09H03: Note 38 describes the combatants armed with iron tiger-like claws tied to their waists.
shots.B15C039S09H04: Note 39 compares the term suradevata with two other terms, karivringhati and govalivardda.
shots.B15C039S09H05: Note 40 says Ulupi is implied in the text.
shots.B15C039S10H01: Note 41 says the text points to the unfairness of a warrior on a car attacking one on foot.
shots.B15C039S10H02: Note 42 says Yudhishthira and Vidura share the same essence of Dharma, so Vidura's entry into Yudhishthira strengthened him.
shots.B15C039S10H03: Note 43 explains keka as the peacock's cry only and describes the datyuha as a bird with a repeated call.
shots.B15C039S10H04: Note 44 defines the copper vessel, the blanket, and the two kinds of ladles.
shots.B15C039S10H05: Note 45 explains that a curse costs a Brahmin some penance, and that Mandavya's curse forced Dharma to accept youth as a plea in judging offences.
shots.B15C039S11H01: Note 46 explains dharana and dhyana as two stages of Yoga, fixing the mind on one thing and withdrawing it from surrounding objects.
shots.B15C039S11H02: Note 47 says Valhika was the father of Somadatta and grandfather of Bhurisravas, and so the grandfather-in-law of the lady Gandhari mentions.
shots.B15C039S11H03: Note 48 says the power meant is the yogin's ability to make himself minute and similar powers.
shots.B15C039S11H04: Note 49 explains that the gods in this passage had taken human form and died in human life.
shots.B15C039S11H05: Note 50 explains the religion of withdrawal from action, which is set against the religion of active works, and says embodied souls enjoy or suffer by the acts of the active religion.
shots.B15C039S12H01: Note 51 explains the mirror image: the soul is like a mirror, and pleasure and pain are reflections that do not change it.
shots.B15C039S12H02: Note 52 says ordinary people take the body for the self, while a wise man whose acts are spent does not, and is freed from taking a body again.
shots.B15C039S12H03: Note 53 says that in ordinary people the body dissolves, while yogins can keep its parts from dissolving.
shots.B15C039S12H04: Note 54 says the gods carry the life-breaths and senses of sacrificed animals to the next world, even though their bodies are destroyed.
shots.B15C039S12H05: Note 55 says lost wives and similar bonds cause sorrow, so the wise avoid forming them.
shots.B15C039S13H01: Note 56 explains the term paraparajnah for a person who knows the difference between body and self, and says that worship of saguna Brahma leads on to nirguna Brahma.
shots.B15C039S13H02: Note 57 says the sense is that beings arise from the unmanifest and return to it, and that the text is hard to construe in places.
shots.B15C039S13H03: Note 58 explains that acts done in the body are enjoyed in the body and acts done mentally are enjoyed mentally.
shots.B15C039S13H04: The translator says the rendering is tentative, a verbal rendering whose chain of reasoning is not clear.
shots.B15C039S13H05: Note 59 says a Bengal reading is wrong and should be punah.
shots.B15C039S14H01: Note 60 explains the grammar of the phrase about circling the king, with a word understood.
shots.B15C039S14H02: Note 61 explains vikarshanam as emaciation from giving up all food.
shots.B15C039S14H03: Note 62 explains that the verb anvacat governs two objects here.
shots.B15C039S14H05: The connecting word of the title line.
shots.B15C039S15H01: Attribution line naming Krishna-Dwaipayana Vyasa as the author.
